title: Lease-driven timebound demotion for KV shards to optimize GPU memory and correctness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: GPU memory fragmentation from KV cache entries and uncoordinated evictions causes tail latency spikes and correctness edge cases during continuous batching. Existing LRU/TTL-only strategies either over-evict hot prefixes or leave stale allocations reserved, increasing OOM risk on multi-tenant Dedicated pools.

Goal: Implement a lease-driven, timebound demotion pipeline for KV shards that (1) reduces noisy eviction-driven batch latency, (2) preserves per-prefix correctness invariants during demotion/eviction, and (3) minimizes peak GPU memory usage via shard-aware demotion tiers and compaction-friendly alignment. The solution must present formal correctness guarantees (no stale reads, no double-free) for interplay with continuous batching and prefetch flows.
design_decisions: Introduce a 3-state lifecycle per KV slice: ACTIVE -> DEMOTED (soft-freed) -> EVICTED (physical free).
Lease token: borrowers (inflight batches / prefetch workers) take ephemeral leases with expiry timestamps; leases are coarse-grained to shard-level to avoid per-entry contention.
Demotion vs eviction: DEMOTED retains metadata on host but releases GPU slab pointers; EVICTED clears metadata and decrements accounting. This allows warm rehydration without immediate reclaim cost.
Shard scoring: eviction candidate ranking blends LRU score, TTL score, prefix-affinity penalty, and fragmentation heuristics to favor contiguous slab reclamation.

Atomic transition guarantees: use epoched CAS across metadata+lease counters so a race between batch pin and demotion results in one of deterministic outcomes (batch wins -> lease extends, demotion wins -> caller receives a retry signal).

Integration with continuous batching: batches consult a lease-check API before finalizing KV pins. If a demotion is in-flight, the batch either waits up to lease_timeout or routes to fallback model variant.
Auditability: snapshot log of demotion/eviction events with per-prefix tags for postmortem correctness checks and provenance in Console.
Backwards compatibility: feature gated behind runtime-1.24 and toggled by per-customer mem-pressure policies for Dedicated/Private tiers.
Fallbacks: fall back to strict LRU single-phase evictions if the epoch CAS implementation proves unstable under stress.
Security/ownership: lease tokens are tied to worker IDs and cannot be forged; audit logs record lease grants/renewals/releases.
Safety margins: enforce per-shard reserved floor to avoid full depletion during compaction anomalies (configurable as percent of shard capacity).
acceptance_criteria: Correctness: under unit/integration tests and fuzz harnesses, no stale read is ever observed after a successful pin (assert linearizability of pin/get semantics).
Performance: under benchmark 50/50 read/write continuous-batching workload, 95th percentile request latency increases by <= 5% compared to baseline and eviction churn decreases by >= 25%.
Memory: peak GPU memory usage for multi-tenant Dedicated sim scenario reduced by >= 12% due to compaction-friendly demotions.
Observability: Console exposes demotion/ejection rate, per-prefix demotion counts, and a demotion-to-eviction latency histogram.
Rollback: ability to toggle feature at runtime with safe draining (no in-flight lease loss leading to incorrect reads).
Security: security review completed and signed-off prior to runtime-1.24 rollout.
Test coverage: end-to-end tests including: lease expiry race, batch pin during demotion, forced crash during demotion, and cross-shard compaction concurrency.
Docs: design doc and runbook published in Confluence; Console docs updated for new metrics and troubleshooting steps.

Test harness: extend fuzzing harness with lease expiry scenarios and randomized batch interleavings (owner: Rafal Kowalski)
Metrics + Console: add demotion/eject metrics and per-prefix tagging (owner: Simone Li)
PRs + Code review: create PRs and implement feedback (owner: Miguel)
Staged rollout: dogfood on internal Dedicated, then limited-customer ramp (owner: SRE team)
Security review: coordinate with security for token model review (owner: Asha)
metrics: pin_retry_rate (percent of pins that observe demotion and must retry)
risk_and_mitigation: Race between batch pin and demotion leading to potential double-free: mitigated by epoched CAS and lease extension path; add integration test that asserts no double-free under adversarial scheduler.
Lease storm: many workers repeatedly renewing leases could block eviction; introduce exponential backoff + jitter and shard-level lease caps to bound renewals.
Fragmentation regression: demotions could create small islands of free memory; enforce compaction trigger when fragmentation ratio > threshold.
Telemetry overload: high-cardinality prefix tags could stress metrics pipeline; sample prefix tags above a cardinality threshold and surface top offenders instead.
Incorrect fallback behavior during toggle: add a draining step that refuses new demotions and waits for leases to expire before toggling off.
Security: forged lease tokens - mitigate by signing tokens and enforcing worker ID checks and KMS-backed signing keys.
